title: Set a digital multimeter to OFF
instruction: Turn the multimeter dial counter-clockwise to OFF.
context: Returning a handheld meter to OFF is a routine test-bench shutdown step that prevents unnecessary battery drain. This task isolates manipulation of a shallow, narrow selector handle among adjacent controls; it does not simulate electrical testing or circuit isolation.
setup: Fixed original calibrated YAM station: two six-axis arms with parallel grippers at bases (0, +0.305, 0.750) m and (0, -0.305, 0.750) m; oak-coloured rigid table 1.10 x 1.30 x 0.06 m, centred at (0.36, 0, 0.7175) m with top at z=0.7475 m; grey floor, top and wrist cameras, camera stand and fixed lighting. One NVIDIA testingTool digital multimeter assembly is the only task asset: grey plastic face, blue rubber-like surround, black plastic dial, and fixed red/black insulated leads with metal probe parts. The case is approximately 185.8 x 88.3 x 40.4 mm; the complete assembly including leads spans approximately 187.1 x 336.1 x 40.5 mm. Its complete horizontal bounding-box centre starts at (0.30, 0.0) m with 180-degree Z yaw. The case is secured to the table by an abstract underside fixture. The dial is 43.9 mm across; its narrow raised handle reaches about 2.6 mm above the spindle-frame origin. The spindle starts at (0.308992, -0.123923, 0.785015) m, and the dial starts at 0 degrees relative to its initial orientation. OFF is the +115-degree counter-clockwise stop. Both arms start in the native READY configuration; exact model geometry, camera calibration and placements are supplied in code.
scoring: Let a be the signed counter-clockwise dial rotation in degrees from reset. A valid dial has its bounding-box centre within 5 mm of the spindle and its local Z axis within 5 degrees of vertical. An invalid/dislodged dial scores 0. Otherwise partial credit is 0.95 * clamp(a / 115, 0, 1), capped at 0.95. Full credit 1.0 is awarded only when the native success termination confirms |a-115| <= 3 degrees, linear speed < 0.005 m/s and angular speed < 0.05 rad/s for 2 consecutive seconds. Trial score uses the final state, not the best intermediate state.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps at 20 Hz (120 seconds simulated time); the scripted demonstration is capped at 600 steps.
reset_notes: Reset the dial and both arms to their initial poses; reset the one-way lower stop to 0 degrees. Nothing is consumed. Use object_jitter=0 for the fixed layout, base seed 0, and the native derived reset seed 1415158438. Keep the meter secured and the leads/accessories in the supplied fixed layout.
fidelity: Original YAM station and NVIDIA visuals. Casing/leads are fixed; the underside fixture is abstract. The dial is a passive Z hinge with an ideal bearing and no casing contact. A software one-way stop enforces the CCW-only rule (0.5 deg backlash), not a stock meter feature. Convex collision and friction are approximate, not hardware-calibrated. Turning uses finger contact, without a motor or grasp weld. Buttons, display, electronics, cable flex and detents are not simulated.
scores: Dream-1 recorded attempt: 0.0 when rounded (raw endpoint task_score 3.653309948503014e-10), scored by post-hoc replay of 1,014 recorded applied actions after manual interruption; the original aggregate score is unavailable. Scripted demonstration: 1.0, native success termination after 352 actions.
